    AI Overview
    Erectile dysfunction (ED), commonly known as impotence, is the persistent inability to achieve or maintain a firm erection for sexual intercourse. Affecting roughly half of men between 40-70, it is often caused by physical issues like diabetes, heart disease, or reduced blood flow, but can also stem from psychological factors such as stress or anxiety. 
    Usage Examples & Signs of ED 
    • Physical Symptoms: Reduced firmness or frequency of morning erections, inability to maintain an erection, and reduced sexual desire (libido).
    • Causes: High-fat diets, excessive alcohol consumption, and chronic health conditions like diabetes, hypertension, and low testosterone.
    • Treatments:
      Common interventions include oral medications (Viagra, Cialis, Levitra, Stendra), vacuum erection devices (penis pumps), testosterone therapy, or psychological counseling.
       
    Synonyms and Related Terms 
    • Impotence: The most direct medical synonym for erectile dysfunction.
    • Erection problems: Commonly used to describe the condition.
    • Sexual dysfunction: A broader term covering ED.
    • Psychogenic ED: Specific to ED caused by stress, anxiety, or depression. 
    Key Facts 
    • ED affects 5-10% of men under 40, while up to 80% of men in their 80s report some degree of the condition.
    • It is often a symptom of underlying health issues rather than just a psychological problem.
    • Common treatments include lifestyle changes, such as quitting smoking, and medication, which usually take effect within an hour.

    What exactly causes ED?
    Organic ED involves abnormalities the penile arteries, veins, or both and is the most common cause of ED, especially in older men. When the problem is arterial, it is usually caused by arteriosclerosis, or hardening of the arteries, although trauma to the arteries may be the cause.
